Development of an Operational Hailstorm Forecasting Methodology for the Indian Region

Abstract:

Forecasting hailstorms is a challenging task due to their large spatial variability during a single event, some areas may experience hail, while others may experience only rainfall. Accurate forecasting is necessary as they cause loss of life, property and agriculture. Currently, IMD does not have any specialised products for hailstorm forecasting, and many publicly available weather platforms also do not provide hailstorm warnings. Forecasters rely on various stability indices, and based on synoptic conditions, they generate predictions based on available parameters to detect the hailstorm formation. Some forecasters try to generate hailstorm predictions from Doppler weather radar data, with limited success, and this approach is only suitable for nowcast warnings of less than three hours. Understanding pre-convective conditions is a prerequisite the thermodynamic indices need to be evaluated before the event begins. Thunderstorms lead to the formation of hail hence, assessing the processes that induce hail formation is required. The existing forecasting systems have poor skill at predicting these events, making it challenging to determine whether an event will be a hailstorm or only a thunderstorm. Therefore, in this work we focus on understanding upper air dynamics and thermodynamics of these events, which helps to improve the prediction skills. The stability indices viz., CAPE, Showalter Index (SI), K Index, Total Totals Index (TTI), Severe Weather Threat Index (SWEAT), Storm Relative Helicity (SRH), Lifted Index (LI), Freezing level, Deep Convective Index (DCI), Energy Helicity Index (EHI), etc., will be evaluated. First, we will identify the frequent hailstorm regions over Uttar Pradesh and adjacent regions based on available observations and reanalysis datasets. We will assess the frequency and spatial variability of these events over the last two decades for the pre-monsoon and post-monsoon seasons. Further, the identified events will be evaluated to understand the dynamical and thermodynamic processes driving hail formation. Based on a comprehensive analysis, we will develop a robust methodology for predicting hailstorm events.
